title: UK CCS AI Procurement Model Clauses 2026 — What Public Buyers Must Ask
context: 2026-08-26 EAT cycle — Crown Commercial Service published AI-specific model contract clauses (July 2026); UK public-sector AI procurement now requires transparency, fairness, and accountability schedules
body: In July 2026, the Crown Commercial Service (CCS) issued model contract clauses for AI procurement by UK public bodies. These clauses apply to any central government department, NHS trust, or local authority buying an AI system — whether a classification model, a generative tool, or an automated decision-making service. The core requirements: (1) the supplier must provide a transparency schedule describing the model's training data lineage, performance characteristics, and known limitations; (2) a fairness schedule documenting bias testing methodology and results disaggregated by protected characteristics under the Equality Act 2010; (3) an accountability schedule identifying the human-in-the-loop decision points and the escalation path for contested automated decisions; (4) a right-to-audit clause allowing the buyer (or its independent auditor) to inspect the system's boundary instrumentation and incident logs. For a verification-first operator, the CCS model clauses align precisely with the Council of AI's verified measurement credential: instead of negotiating bespoke schedules per contract, the supplier publishes a signed, auditable measurement record that satisfies the transparency and accountability schedules in a single artifact. The posture is monitored containment applied to public procurement: the question is not 'Does this AI system never fail?' but 'Do we have instrumented boundaries and independent verification that failure will be detected and reported?'.
